Away from the ends, the curve C_0 is identified canonically with C_alpha, and this identification extends holomorphically to a (non-injective) map from C_0 to C_alpha defined outside the S^1times[4S,infty) subsets of the ends. Thus there is a well-defined such W^k-1,2,delta,delta space of sections on C_0 defined outside the S^1times[4S,infty) subsets of the ends, valued in Omega^0,1_tilde C_0,j_yotimes_mathbb C u_0|alpha^ast TM_J(ell_alpha,w(A_y(cdot))). Now, for instance, the middle horizontal map D_alpha,w,y can be seen as giving a section in this W^k-1,2,delta,delta space defined outside S^1times[4S,infty). In the proof below, it is convenient to use this W^k-1,2,delta,delta space of sections defined outside S^1times[4S,infty), though we must be careful that the expressions we write are well-defined. Finally, let us define the map: W^k-1,2,delta,delta(tilde C_0,Omega^0,1_tilde C_0,j_yotimes_mathbb C u_0|alpha^ast TM_J(ell_alpha,w(A_y(cdot))))xrightarrowglueW^k-1,2,delta,delta(tilde C_alpha,Omega^0,1_tilde C_alpha,j_yotimes_mathbb C u_alpha^ast TM_J(ell_alpha,w(A_y(cdot)))) Let etain W^k-1,2,delta,delta(tilde C_0,Omega^0,1_tilde C_0,j_yotimes_mathbb C u_0|alpha^ast TM_J(ell_alpha,w(A_y(cdot)))). Away from the necks of C_alpha, glue(eta) is simply eta. In any particular bubble neck S^1times[0,6S]subseteq C_alpha, we define: glue(eta)(t,s):= eta(t,s)&sleq 2Scr chi(4S-s)eta(t,s)+chi(4S-s')eta(t',s')&2Sleq sleq 4Scr eta(t',s')&4Sleq s (this definition also applies over the main necks with the obvious adjustment). Note that gluecircbreak' is the identity map. Now suppose that D_0|alpha,0,yxi=break(eta); we must show that: left\|D_alpha,w,y(glue(xi))-etaright\|_k-1,2,delta,deltaleq ccdotbigl(left|alpharight|^epsilon+left|wright|bigr)left\|xiright\|_k,2,delta,delta Using the triangle inequality and the fact that eta=glue(break'(eta))=glue(id^1,0(D_0|alpha,0,yxi)), we conclude that left\|D_alpha,w,y(glue(xi))-etaright\| is bounded above by: left\|D_alpha,w,y(glue(xi))-glue(D_alpha,w,y(xi))right\|+left\|glueleft[D_alpha,w,y(xi)-id^1,0(D_0|alpha,0,y(xi))right]right\| We now estimate each term separately. To estimate left\|D_alpha,w,y(glue(xi))-glue(D_alpha,w,y(xi))right\|, argue as follows. The difference is only nonzero over the regions S^1times([2S,2S+1]cup[4S-1,4S]) of each neck. Now the norm is bounded by left\|xiright\|e^-2Sdelta (calculation left to the reader), where the factor of e^-2Sdelta comes as the ratio of the weight given to S^1times[4S-1,4S] inside a neck vs inside an end; this gives the desired bound since delta>0. To estimate left\|glueleft[D_alpha,w,y(xi)-id^1,0(D_0|alpha,0,yxi)right]right\|, argue as follows. This is bounded by a constant times the (k-1,2,delta,delta)-norm of D_alpha,w,y(xi)-id^1,0(D_0|alpha,0,yxi) over the complement of the subsets S^1times[4S,infty) of the ends. Now this is bounded by (left|alpharight|^epsilon+left|wright|)left\|xiright\|_k,2,delta,delta using the reasoning from Lemma .

\end{equation}

To bound left\|partial_sxiright\|_2^2, we write: left\|partial_sxiright\|_2&=left\|Jpartial_txi+A(xi)partial_txi+Q(xi)right\|_2cr &geqleft\|Jpartial_txiright\|_2-left\|A(xi)partial_txiright\|_2-left\|Q(xi)right\|_2cr &geqleft\|Jpartial_txiright\|_2-left\|A(xi)right\|_inftyleft\|partial_txiright\|_2-cleft\|xiright\|_inftyleft\|xiright\|_2cr &=left\|Jpartial_txiright\|_2-o(1)left\|Jpartial_txiright\|_2-o(1)left\|xiright\|_2geq(1-o(1))deltaleft\|xiright\|_2 and thus left\|partial_sxiright\|_2^2geq(1-o(1))delta^2f(s). nodes.statement: To identify the orientation sheaf of overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q) with mathfrak o_sigmaotimesmathfrak o_p,q, it suffices to identify the orientation sheaf of every overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^reg with mathfrak o_E_Iotimesmathfrak o_sigmaotimesmathfrak o_p,q in a compatible way (for all finite subsets Isubseteqmathcal A(sigma,p,q)^geqmathfrak s^top). Moreover, it suffices to make this identification over the open subset overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^regcircsubseteqoverlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^reg where the domain curve is smooth (it then automatically extends uniquely to all of overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^reg, by virtue of the local topological description of overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^reg given by the gluing map); we may also check compatibility with the inclusions Isubseteq J over overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^regcirc. Now the kernel tilde K=ker D of the linearization forms a vector bundle over overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^regcirc, and the orientation sheaf of overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^regcirc is isomorphic to mathfrak o_sigmaotimesmathfrak o_tilde K (to see this, one must distinguish the two cases dimsigma>0 and dimsigma=0). Now we have mathfrak o_tilde K=mathfrak o_D=mathfrak o_D_hol=mathfrak o_E_Iotimesmathfrak o_p,q; this defines a fiberwise isomorphism of mathfrak o_tilde K with mathfrak o_E_Iotimesmathfrak o_p,q, and since the operators D and D_hol vary nicely over the base overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^regcirc, it is easy to see that this is in fact an isomorphism of sheaves. Thus we have the desired identification. Now let us show that the boundary map induced by coincides with the tautological map (this just amounts to chasing definitions). Let mathfrak sinmathcal S_overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q) denote the stratum (sigma|[0ldotshat kldots n],p,q) (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of trajectories over sigma which factor through sigma|[0ldotshat kldots n]). Now on the space overlinemathcal M(sigma|[0ldotshat kldots n],p,q)=overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)^leqmathfrak s, we have three implicit atlases: mathcal A(sigma|[0ldotshat kldots n],p,q)^geqmathfrak s^topsubseteqmathcal A(sigma,p,q)^geqmathfrak ssupseteqmathcal A(sigma,p,q)^geqmathfrak s^top (note that the two occurences of mathfrak s^top refer to the top elements of two different strata posets); in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left. The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaf of overlinemathcal M(sigma|[0ldotshat kldots n],p,q)=overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)^leqmathfrak s under the leftmost implicit atlas applies equally well for all three atlases (and, in particular, the resulting identifications coincide). Hence, for the purpose of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas mathcal A(sigma,p,q)^geqmathfrak s^top on overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q) and the inclusion of the boundary stratum overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)^leqmathfrak shookrightarrowoverlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q). Now it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion (overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)^leqmathfrak s_I)^regcirchookrightarrowoverlinemathcal M(sigma,p,q)_I^regcirc (for all finite subsets Isubseteqmathcal A(sigma,p,q)^geqmathfrak s^top), and this follows by definition. Now let us show that the boundary map induced by coincides with the tautological map . First, we chase definitions as above. Let mathfrak sinmathcal S_overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r) denote the stratum (sigma|[0ldots k],p,q)--(sigma|[kldots n],q,r) (i.e.\ the stratum consisting of Floer trajectories over sigma which are broken at vertex k and periodic orbit qinmathcal P_H(k)). Now on the space overlinemathcal M(sigma|[0ldots k],p,q)timesoverlinemathcal M(sigma|[kldots n],q,r)=overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)^leqmathfrak s, we have three implicit atlases: mathcal A(sigma|[0ldots k],p,q)^geqmathfrak s^topsqcupmathcal A(sigma|[kldots n],q,r)^geqmathfrak s^topsubseteqmathcal A(sigma,p,r)^geqmathfrak ssupseteqmathcal A(sigma,p,r)^geqmathfrak s^top and in fact (the index set of) the middle atlas is the disjoint union of (the index sets of) the atlases on the right and on the left. The reasoning used above to identify the orientation sheaves of overlinemathcal M(sigma|[0ldots k],p,q) and overlinemathcal M(sigma|[kldots n],q,r) applies equally well to identify the orientation sheaf of their product overlinemathcal M(sigma|[0ldots k],p,q)timesoverlinemathcal M(sigma|[kldots n],q,r)=overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)^leqmathfrak s under all three atlases above (the fact that the thickening datums in the latter two atlases do not treat the portions of the trajectories from p to q and from q to r ``independently'' does not cause any problems). Hence for the purposes of identifying the boundary map on orientation sheaves, it suffices to consider the single atlas mathcal A(sigma,p,r)^geqmathfrak s^top on overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r) and the inclusion of the boundary stratum overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)^leqmathfrak shookrightarrowoverlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r). As before, it suffices to check that the desired compatibility holds for the inclusion (overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)^leqmathfrak s_I)^reghookrightarrowoverlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)_I^reg (for all finite subsets Isubseteqmathcal A(sigma,p,r)^geqmathfrak s^top), and moreover, this may be checked on the locus where the domain curve is smooth except for the required node over k asymptotic to qinmathcal P_H(k). It will be convenient to assume that 0<k<n, so let us first deduce the case of general 0leq kleq n from the case 0<k<n. Fix sigma and 0leq kleq n=dimsigma. We consider the degenerate simplex sigma'tosigma given by ``doubling vertex 0'' if k=0 and ``doubling vertex n'' if k=n (i.e.\ if 0=k<n, we consider Delta^n+1toDelta^n given by superimposing the first two vertices of Delta^n+1, if 0<k=n, we consider Delta^n+1toDelta^n given by superimposing the last two vertices of Delta^n+1, and if 0=k=n we consider Delta^2toDelta^0); let k'=1 if k=0 and let k'=n'-1 if k=n, where n'=dimsigma', and note that 0<k'<n'. Now there is a natural map mathcal A(sigma,p,q)^geqmathfrak s^toptomathcal A(sigma',p,q)^geqmathfrak s^top given by pulling back along sigma'tosigma, and sigma'tosigma maps flow lines to flow lines (for the flow from Definition ). Hence, given any point xinoverlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)_I^reg with a single node over k asymptotic to qinmathcal P_H(k), we may lift it (canonically, up to translating the part(s) of the trajectory over 0=k and/or over k=n) to a point x'inoverlinemathcal M(sigma',p,r)_I^reg with a single node over k' asymptotic to qinmathcal P_H'(k')=mathcal P_H(k). To review: we have identified the orientation sheaf of overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)_I^reg with mathfrak o_E_Iotimesmathfrak o_sigmaotimesmathfrak o_p,r, and we have identified the orientation sheaf of (overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)^leqmathfrak s_I)^reg with mathfrak o_E_Iotimesmathfrak o_sigma|[0ldots k]otimesmathfrak o_p,qotimesmathfrak o_sigma|[kldots n]otimesmathfrak o_q,r (recall that mathfrak s denotes the stratum consisting of trajectories broken at vertex k and periodic orbit qinmathcal P_H(k)). We consider the gluing setup for overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)_I^reg at a point in (overlinemathcal M(sigma,p,r)^leqmathfrak s_I)^reg where C_0 is smooth except for the required node over vertex k asymptotic to qinmathcal P_H(k). In other words, C_0setminus\q_0,q_1,q_2\=S^1timesmathbb Rsqcup S^1timesmathbb R, and u_0:S^1timesmathbb Rsqcup S^1timesmathbb Rto M is a trajectory from p to q and from q to r.
